description: Divergences the randomized differential run (crates/sandbox-conformance/tests/differential.rs) found between clients or against the filesystem, each as a permanent check. A check marked xfail for a driver is a known defect of that client; a fix removes the mark and the matching entry in tests/differential/known.rs.

scenarios.description: A write below a regular file fails with not_found or not_a_directory, whatever characters the name has. The failing command's stderr is `sh: N: cannot create PATH: Directory nonexistent`; the kind comes from the first line up to LF. A name containing CR (or another character Python's splitlines() breaks at) must not move the OS message out of that line.

xfail.reason: the Python client reads the first stderr line with str.splitlines(), which also splits at this character; FILES-OVER-EXEC 3.3 reads up to LF, so the OS error is missed and the kind falls back to io

scenarios.description: A file called .git whose content is not UTF-8, in a directory above the search root, does not make the search fail. ripgrep reads the nearest .git as a gitdir pointer, complains on stderr (`stream did not contain valid UTF-8`) and exits 2; the line is not a per-path OS error, so the clients report invalid_query although the pattern is fine and the matches were printed.

args: set -e; cd "$1"; mkdir sub; printf 'nothing here\n' > sub/x.txt; printf '\377\376 not utf8\n' > .git

xfail.reason: rg's complaint about the unreadable .git file above the root is not an OS error, so its exit 2 reads as a rejected pattern
